listenings.text: People assume that stage fright is something you grow out of, and I am here to tell you that it is not. I have been doing this for nineteen years and I still go blank in the wings about twice a season. What changes is not the fear. What changes is what you do with it. When I was twenty I used to arrive four minutes before the call, no warm-up, nothing, because I thought preparation was for people without talent. That is exactly how I lost a whole page of the script in front of six hundred people. I stood there, I could see the other actor waiting for the cue, and there was simply nothing in my head. So now I do the boring thing. I get backstage an hour early, I warm up my voice for fifteen minutes even when I feel ridiculous doing it, and I read the first two pages out loud to myself. And here is the part nobody tells you when you are starting: the actors who look the calmest are almost never the ones who feel the calmest. They are the ones who built a routine and stopped negotiating with it.

Hello, and thank you for calling the Riverside Community Theater. Our office is closed right now, but this message has everything you need about open auditions, so please listen all the way through. We are casting our March production and auditions run on Tuesday the third and Wednesday the fourth, from six in the evening until half past nine. No appointment is needed on Tuesday. Wednesday is by appointment only, so if Wednesday is your only option, send us an email first. You do not need experience and you do not need to bring a photograph. Please do prepare one short piece, about two minutes, and learn it by heart, because we will ask you to do it twice, the second time with a different instruction. Come at least twenty minutes early so you can warm up properly. And one thing we say every year, because every year somebody is caught by it: if you have not performed in a while and you feel rusty, come anyway. Half the cast of our last show had not been on a stage in over five years. Auditions are held at the back entrance on Willow Street, not the main door.
